memo.verdict: Progress AMBU.B-DK (Ambu A/S) to Early-Stage Assessment on moderate conviction, explicitly as a research decision and explicitly not as a capital decision. The memo adopts the Risks report's capital instruction in full and departs from it only on research progression, on the ground that the report's stated object is "a concentrated long-only portfolio", which is the Live stage, not Triaging. Two conditions bind the progression. Condition one: Early-Stage Assessment must open on the false-friend guardrail, testing cash conversion, working capital and capitalised development against reported margin before any valuation work. Condition two: the Q3 FY2025/26 print must be read into the memo, specifically for urology organic growth and the tariff line, because both are the named swing factors. The memo states that if the Q3 FY2025/26 print shows urology decelerating again alongside a further legacy decline, the progression recommendation should be withdrawn at the next cycle. Element E8 (Fit with acceptable case setups) identifies the primary setup fit as Required Attribute 2 (big demand change-driven earnings-per-share upgrade or expansion) and the secondary fit as Required Attribute 5 (huge change-from-current clearing event in solid quality). Both carve-outs deepen at Early-Stage Assessment.
case: The Triaging stage test asks whether the case carries large amounts of positive change forces, and on the memo's evidence it plainly does. That is the spine of the recommendation.

External change force. The reusable-to-single-use conversion is an early-stage structural shift with decades of runway. Single-use is only 3% to 4% of a DKK 190bn global endoscopy market, growing above 20% a year against 6% for reusables, with one projection at a 27% rate through 2030. Clinicians expect eventual penetration near 70% in respiratory, urology and ear-nose-throat, against 20%, 15% and 4% today, so the least-converted pools are the largest. The clinical economics are quantified rather than asserted: single-use cystoscopy delivers a 50% increase in patient throughput, cuts patient transition time by 34%, and delivers 13% cost savings in bronchoscopy and 10% in cystoscopy net of the higher unit price.

Internal change force. ZOOM AHEAD, launched 1 October 2025, raised the five-year organic growth target to 11% to 13% from above 10%, with Endoscopy Solutions at 15% to 20% and the legacy division raised to 3% to 5% from 2% to 4%. The margin ambition is above 20% by FY2029/30 against 13.0% delivered in FY2024/25 and 2.7% in FY2021/22. The memo's specific point is that this is change layered on a completed turnaround, not remedial change responding to failure, which is the reason Element E1 Required Attribute 1 grades B rather than C. The contrast drawn against the peer set is Coloplast, whose Impact4 plan lowered its target.
counter_case: The Risks report's own stage verdict. The memo quotes it twice and adopts both quotations in full as capital instructions. First: "we recommend letting the investment idea sit rather than progressing it into a concentrated long-only portfolio". Second: "we recommend a hold-and-watch stance until the next two quarterly reports verify the urology commercial acceleration". The memo's departure is on scope alone, arguing that Triaging decides research progression and the report's stated object is the concentrated long-only portfolio. The memo explicitly records that this is a genuine disagreement to note rather than argue away: "a reader could reasonably read 'letting the investment idea sit' as park at any stage, and that reading is recorded here rather than argued away".

The false-friend guardrail fires. Element E8 Required Attribute 8 grades D. The Risks report's competing-hypotheses matrix across fifteen evidence items returns one hard inconsistency for the FALSE FRIEND profile against seven for the YES profile and five for the NO profile. Four independently measurable indicators corroborate it. Operating cash flow was depressed by a DKK 273m working-capital outflow in FY2024/25, with net working capital at 22% of revenue against a 20% target. Cash conversion before acquisitions fell to 35% from 52% while margins rose, which the memo calls the precise signature this guardrail exists to catch. Development costs of DKK 267m were capitalised in the year, with DKK 596m of gastroenterology intangibles still carried after the earlier DKK 334m impairment. Monitor bundling at low gross margin and seasonal respiratory demand are both named as mechanisms that flatter reported volume against underlying cash. The memo holds the grade at D rather than F because free cash flow was still positive at DKK 407m and the transmission mechanism from scope volume to consumable revenue to gross margin is clear and traceable, which a textbook false friend lacks.
triggers: Six carried questions, ranked by decision weight in the memo. One: does the 60% single-use volume share survive contact with sub-cost entry, or does the standard-scope segment commoditise as the bear case argues. Two: is the reported margin recovery in the second half genuine operating leverage, or an artefact of tariff phasing that reverses when the phasing normalises. Three: does cash conversion return above the company's own 40% target once the inventory build unwinds, or is the 35% reading structural. Four: is the DKK 596m of gastroenterology intangible book value recoverable, given the earlier DKK 334m impairment on the same asset base. Five: what is the realistic landing zone for the FY2027/28 margin, given the 250 basis-point gap between the company's 20% reference and the aggregated sell-side 17.5%. Six: does the absence of any financial currency hedging warrant a valuation discount.

Triggers that would withdraw the progression recommendation. A second consecutive urology deceleration; a further guidance narrowing; or evidence that the Mexican transfer is slipping. Each would invalidate the progression case independently. The memo states plainly that if the Q3 FY2025/26 print shows urology decelerating again alongside a further legacy decline, the recommendation should be withdrawn at the next cycle.

Triggers that would raise conviction to high. Tariff refunds landing; urology reaccelerating above 18%, the rolling twelve-month rate the sources cite as the recent trend; and cash conversion recovering above 40%. Together these would convert the case into a high-conviction clearing-event case.

Reassessment criteria if parked instead. Two consecutive quarters of urology organic growth above 18%; the quarterly tariff charge falling materially below the DKK 52m level, evidencing the Mexican transfer working as described; and a refreshed risks family report revising or reaffirming the false-friend finding against post-print evidence.

Standing monitorables named in the memo. United States customs import volumes for competing cystoscopes each quarter, described as the earliest available competitive signal. Average selling prices in North American cystoscopy, the named early-warning indicator for commoditisation in the business-foundations work. A persistent fall in respiratory organic growth below 10%, the sources' own earliest warning on bronchoscopy price erosion. Gross margin, as the single cleanest transmission point for the oil-price thematic. The quarterly tariff charge, as the cleanest test of the Mexican transfer.

Research-coverage gaps carried forward. No leadership-foundations family exists on disk, confirmed by direct folder listing; this will block Element E9 (Great operator) at Early-Stage Assessment and must be commissioned first. The risks family report predates the Q2 FY2025/26 print commentary and needs refreshing. The assembled coverage note records "Above-floor reports present: none", which is wrong, since three above-floor families are present and were read; this should be corrected at source. Three of the four active thematics were last substantively reviewed in April 2026 and are marked carried forward, not re-reviewed, so Element E5 and MR3 should be re-run when they are refreshed.
